newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher, led by September.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher, led by September.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled higher, with September gaining on continued talk of planting delays in the northern U.S. Plains because of the risk of spring flooding, traders said.

"I think a lot of this was lingering concern about flooding. Everybody's talking about that. The thing is, I don't think there's much fresh news about the floods -- it's just that there isn't much for sale," an MGE trader said.
"If you want to buy 100,000 (bushels of Sept wheat), you're going to have to chase the market higher," the trader said.

MGE spring wheat settled three to six cents per bushel higher, with May up 5-1/4 cents at $4.09-1/4. New crop September, which had been trailing all other contracts until late in the session, ended up six cents at $3.97.
Traders said CIS was a featured player, selling one million May bushels.
MGE barley futures did not trade.
